topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These introductory remarks welcome the students and establish the lecture's learning objectives.

topics.label: Viral oncogenesis and experimental transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how the study of tumor viruses led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and the experimental assays used to measure cellular transformation.

topics.label: Cancer gene classifications and tumor suppressor mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the definitions of cancer mutations and demonstrate how pathway regulation and allele dosage modulate oncogenic and tumor-suppressive phenotypes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how defects in DNA repair, replication, and chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability and trigger downstream cellular stress.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how sequential somatic mutation accumulation and inherited gene defects accelerate tumor progression and shape malignancy.

topics.label: Conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: These closing remarks summarise the completed lecture and provide recommended reading for students.
